newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says fighting invading rebels in northeast.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says fighting invading rebels in northeast.

text.p: Sudan said on Monday it was fighting Eritrean and Ethiopian troops that have taken control of border areas in the northeastern Red Sea state.

"Our forces are now advancing on all fronts and are working to clear the border areas this week," the government-owned Sudan al-Hadith newspaper quoted the commissioner of Tokar province, Abdel Rahman Balal, as saying.
"The armed forces and the popular defence force are now clearing the pockets of mercenaries, agents and the minority Ethiopian (troops) amongst the mountains," the daily added.

Sudanese rebels said last week they were mounting a major offensive in the northeast of Africa's largest country and were advancing on Tokar town in the northeast en route to heading towards Port Sudan, a key link with the outside world.
The daily also quoted Red Sea state governor Badawi al-Khair Idris as saying the army was also battling Eritreans and that their counter-attack began two days ago.
Sudan said last week that Eritreans bombed the garrisons but the official's comments are its first admission that the rebels had also taken over the towns.

John Garang, leader of the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) and head of the military command of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) coalition, said rebels seized garrisons at Karora, Itairba and Shabri near the Red Sea coast.
Sudan maintains that Eritrea, Ethiopia and Uganda are fighting alongside the rebels who launched their offensive to topple the government in January.
All three states deny any involvement in the clashes.

Al-Sudan al-Hadith also quoted Balal as saying the Eritreans had looted property, imprisoned local leaders and killed a 70-year-old religious figure. There was no independent confirmation of the report.
